assertions.title: Global shell stays usable across all major routes

steps.action: Open /, /projects, /resume, and /projects/ord-lga-price-war in the shared browser session
steps.expected: Each route keeps working Home/Projects navigation, a keyboard-reachable skip link, and a visible footer
steps.observed: All four routes exposed top-nav Home/Projects links and a visible "Skip to content" link; home, projects, resume, and the sampled case-study route also retained the shared footer with Home/Projects/Resume and contact links.

evidence.network: Browser navigation returned rendered pages for /, /projects, /resume, and /projects/ord-lga-price-war

assertions.title: Home and index expose portfolio-level trust framing before drill-down

steps.action: Inspect home cards and projects index cards before entering a case study
steps.expected: Portfolio surfaces expose evidence level, method/source, and freshness framing up front
steps.observed: Home exposed six case-study cards with decision claim, method + source, and freshness labels; the projects index also exposed trust metadata on cards while filters remained available.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; browser console only showed non-user-facing CSS preload warnings on home/projects
evidence.network: GET / and GET /projects rendered trust-rich card surfaces in browser

assertions.title: Resume page functions as a live credibility surface

steps.action: Open /resume and inspect the top section and supporting sections
steps.expected: Identity, contact actions, quantified highlights, grouped skills, experience history, and labeled PDF download are present
steps.observed: The resume page showed Vaibhav Bapat identity, direct email/contact actions, quantified highlights, skills/experience sections, and labeled PDF resume links.

steps.action: Request the linked PDF resume asset

assertions.title: Production-like runs do not leak dev-only diagnostics

steps.action: Review /, /projects, /resume, and /projects/ord-lga-price-war in the production-like server run
steps.expected: No developer overlay, environment banner, or dev-only warning appears in the user-facing UI
steps.observed: No route displayed a Next.js dev overlay, environment badge, or other developer-only UI. Only browser-console CSS preload warnings appeared, and they were not visible in-page.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; console warnings limited to CSS preload notices on home/projects
evidence.network: Production-like pages rendered from localhost:3501 without dev overlay assets or visible diagnostics

assertions.title: Home hero clearly frames the portfolio as a decision-intelligence product

steps.action: Open / and inspect hero copy and primary calls to action
steps.expected: Landing page communicates portfolio identity, domain breadth, and direct actions to projects and resume
steps.observed: The hero framed the site as a decision-intelligence portfolio and exposed direct Explore Simulators and View Resume actions instead of a generic personal homepage.

evidence.network: GET / -> rendered hero and CTA content

assertions.title: Home project grid enables trust-rich case comparison

steps.action: Inspect the home project grid and extract linked case-study cards
steps.expected: All six case studies are present with decision claim, result, evidence framing, source framing, and detail links
steps.observed: The home route exposed six project cards linking to unique /projects/* routes, and each card included a headline outcome plus decision claim, method + source, and freshness framing for side-by-side trust comparison.

evidence.network: Home card hrefs resolved to six unique case-study destinations under /projects/*

steps.action: Open /projects and inspect available filter groups
steps.expected: Users can filter by domain, evidence level, and output type while trust metadata remains visible
steps.observed: The projects index exposed domain filters (Pricing, Fraud, Retail Ops, Geospatial, Infrastructure, Portfolio), evidence filters (Real, Mixed, Modeled), and output filters (ROI / NPV, ATE, Risk Score, Frontier), while card trust copy remained on the page.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; browser console only showed non-user-facing CSS preload warnings
evidence.network: GET /projects -> rendered six-card library with filter controls

assertions.title: Projects index counts and filters remain internally consistent

steps.action: Record the initial /projects count, then apply Fraud + Modeled filters and inspect visible results
steps.expected: Visible result count updates consistently and remaining card navigation still works
steps.observed: The page began at 6 simulators, then showed 1 of 6 simulators after Fraud + Modeled filtering, leaving only /projects/fraud-radar visible with a clear-all-filters control still available.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; browser console only showed non-user-facing CSS preload warnings
evidence.network: Filtered navigation preserved a valid visible destination: /projects/fraud-radar

assertions.title: Zero-match filter states are explicit and reversible

steps.action: Apply Fraud + Real + Frontier filters to force a zero-result state on /projects
steps.expected: Page shows an explicit empty-state message and a clear way to restore results
steps.observed: The zero-result combination removed all visible project cards and the captured screenshot clearly showed the explicit heading "NO MATCHING PROJECTS", explanatory copy about the filter combination hiding all six case studies, and a visible "RESET FILTERS" action to restore results.

evidence.network: Filtered /projects state rendered with zero visible project links, explicit empty-state copy, and a visible reset affordance in screenshot evidence

frictions.description: agent-browser text capture on Next.js App Router pages included streamed payload/script content after visible UI text, which made exact copy verification noisy on some routes.
frictions.resolution: Used annotated/full-page screenshots plus targeted DOM checks for counts, links, and required labels; final screenshot review provided sufficient evidence to confirm the zero-state message and reset affordance as well.

frictions.description: Browser console on home/projects emitted a CSS preload warning for a preloaded stylesheet that was not used quickly after load.
frictions.resolution: Recorded it as a non-user-facing console warning only; it did not surface as visible dev diagnostics and did not block route validation.

summary: Tested 9 assigned global discovery assertions on the production-like server. All 9 passed: global shell, home hero/grid, resume credibility surface, trust framing, projects discovery/filter consistency, and the zero-match empty-state with reset path all worked as specified.
